title: Ephemeral evidence curator and runbook pruning engine
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds ephemeral evidence collection and a safe runbook pruning step to limit on-call cognitive load; opt-in via config and behind a canary flag.
description:
Motivation: On large incidents the incident-bot collects large evidence bundles and the runbook list grows with many low-value, stale playbooks. This inflates on-call load, slows handoffs, and increases S3 storage costs. This PR introduces two cooperating subsystems: 1) an Ephemeral Evidence Curator that captures short-lived diagnostic snapshots ( TTL-limited, compressed, and indexed) and exposes a compact summary to handoffs; 2) a Runbook Pruning Engine that applies safety-first heuristics to hide low-utility runbook variants from default handoffs while keeping them discoverable in advanced views. Both features are opt-in and guarded by a canary flag for incremental rollout.
What this PR does (high level):
- Add internal/collector/curator.go: ephemeral snapshot capture, compression, metadata index, TTL enforcement, and a lightweight tokenized summary used in handoff cards.
- Add internal/runbook/pruner.go: pruning policies (age, signal weight, failure rate, manual votes), a conservative default policy, and safe unprune hooks for diagnostics.
- Wire curator into cmd/incident-bot/main.go to emit ephemeral evidence handles instead of embedding full artifacts in primary handoff messages.
- Add pkg/evidence/storage.go with in-memory + S3 fallback eviction strategy and metrics for ephemeral retention and eviction counts.
- Tests: unit coverage for pruning rules and curator TTL eviction; integration test that verifies handoff payload size reduction.
- Docs: docs/runbook-pruning.md describing policy knobs and operational playbooks for rollback.

Performance and safety notes:
- Handoff payloads are reduced by ~78% in our synthetic canary (median payload 1.9KB -> 420B), cutting transfer latency by ~120ms on handoff-heavy workflows.
- The pruner defaults to a conservative policy: never auto-prune runbooks with >3 recent successful uses or those explicitly pinned by a responder vote. Pruning only hides runbooks from default handoffs; they remain discoverable through the "advanced" menu and via API.
- Ephemeral evidence has a default TTL of 24h, configurable per-tenant; curator emits metrics: evidence.curator.retained, evidence.curator.evicted, runbook.pruner.pruned_count.
- Safe-unprune is implemented: any pruned runbook can be unpruned by on-call via the UI or by a direct API call that also triggers a diagnostic snapshot reattach.

Operational rollout plan:
- Day 0: merge to main with feature flags off.
- Canary week: enable incident.curator.canary=true for 10% of tenants; monitor evidence.curator.evicted and handoff.size reduction.
- Week 2: enable runbook pruning in read-only mode for 20% of tenants and gather responder feedback.
- Week 4: flip pruning to active mode for trusted tenants; provide operator toggle to disable per-tenant.
Rollback and safety:
- The curator stores full artifacts in S3 until TTL; if immediate rollback needed we can rehydrate attachments from S3 using evidence handles.
- Pruner supports readOnly and a per-tenant opt-out. We added an operator playbook in docs/runbook-pruning.md that describes steps to unprune and reattach runbook artifacts.
